zh: 住在洋场的人，特别是经常在花天酒地中的，都有迟睡迟起的习惯；古应春因为有生意要照料，起得还算早的，但也要九点钟才下床。这天八点钟就有娘姨来敲房门；说号子里派了人来，有话要说。『什么话？』古应春隔着窗子问。『杭州有位刘三爷来。人在号子里。』『哪个刘三爷？』睡眼惺松的古应春，一时想不起是谁。七姑奶奶在后房却想到了，掀开帐子说道∶『不是刘不才刘三爷吗？』『是他？不会是他！』古应春说，『刘三爷也是自己人；一来，当然会到这里来，跑到号子里去干什么？』『老板娘的话不错。』号子里的伙计在窗外接口，『本来是要请刘三爷到家里来的。他说，他身上破破烂烂不好意思来。』果然是刘不才！这个意外的消息，反替古应春带来了迷茫，竟忘了说话。还是七姑奶奶的心思快，胡家的情形还不知道，也许有了什么不幸之事；如果让胡雪岩知道了，一定立刻要见他，当面锣，对面鼓，什么话都瞒不住他，大是不妥。因此，她便替丈夫作主，吩咐伙计先回号子，说古应春马上去看他；同时叮嘱下人，不准在胡雪岩面前透露刘不才已到上海的消息。
en: People in the foreign settlement, particularly those who spent their time in pleasure and revelry, were accustomed to late nights and late mornings. With business to attend to, Gu Yingchun rose comparatively early, but even he did not get out of bed until nine. This morning, at eight, a maid knocked at the bedroom door. Someone had come from the firm with a message. “What message?” Gu asked through the window. “A Third Master Liu has arrived from Hangzhou. He is at the firm.” “Which Third Master Liu?” Still sleepy, Gu could not think who it was. The Seventh Lady, in the inner room, remembered at once. Lifting the bed curtains, she said, “Is it not Liu Bucai—Third Master Liu?” “Him? Surely not. He is one of our own people. He would come straight here. Why go to the firm?” “Madam is right,” the clerk answered from outside the window. “We asked him to come to the house, but he said his clothes were too ragged. He was embarrassed to call.” So it really was Liu Bucai. The unexpected news left Gu bewildered and momentarily speechless. The Seventh Lady thought faster. They still knew nothing of the Hu family’s circumstances; some misfortune might have occurred. If Hu learned that Liu was here, he would insist on seeing him immediately. Face to face, nothing could be concealed from him, and that might be disastrous. She therefore answered for her husband, telling the clerk to return to the firm and say that Gu would be there at once. She also warned the servants not to let Hu know that Liu had arrived in Shanghai.

zh: 『想不到是他来了。』古应春说，『你要不要跟我一道去看他。』『自然要罗！』夫妇俩一辆马车赶到号子里；相见之下，彼此都有片刻的沉默。沉默中，古应春夫妇将刘不才从头看到底，衣衫虽然褴褛，精神气色都还不错，不象是快饿死了的样子。『刘三叔！』终于是七姑奶奶先开口，『你好吧？』『还好，还好！』刘不才仿佛一下子惊醒过来，眨一眨眼说∶『再世做人，又在一起了，自然还好！』听得这话，古应春夫妇不约而同地松了口气，『胡家呢？』七姑奶奶问道，『都好吧？』『逃难苦一点，大大小小轮流生病，现在总算都好了。』『啊——！』七姑奶奶长长舒口气，双手合掌，当胸顶礼∶『谢天谢地。』然后又说∶『不过我倒又不懂了，杭州城里饿死的人无其数——。』说到这里，她咽口唾沫，将最后那句话缩了回去。那句话是个疑问∶饿死的人既然无其数，何以胡家上下一个人都没有饿死？刘不才懂她的意思，但不是一句话所能解释答得了的，『真正菩萨保佑！要谈起来三天三夜说不尽。』
en: “To think that he has come,” Gu said. “Will you go with me?” “Of course!” Husband and wife hurried to the firm together in a carriage. When they met Liu, all three were silent for a moment. Gu and his wife studied him from head to foot. His clothes were ragged, but his spirits and complexion were quite good. He did not look like a man near starvation. “Third Uncle Liu!” The Seventh Lady was the first to speak. “Are you well?” “Well enough, well enough!” Liu seemed suddenly to awaken. Blinking, he said, “Alive for a second time, and together with you again—of course I am well.” Husband and wife both breathed more easily. “And the Hu family?” she asked. “Are they all well?” “Refugee life has been hard. The old and young took turns falling ill, but now they have all recovered.” “Ah!” She let out a long breath and pressed her palms together in thanksgiving. “Thank Heaven!” Then she added, “But now I do not understand. Countless people have starved to death in Hangzhou—” She swallowed the rest. Her unspoken question was plain: if so many had starved, how had every member of the Hu household survived? Liu understood, but no brief answer could explain it. “It was truly the Bodhisattva’s protection. I could not tell it all in three days and nights.”

zh: 他急转直下地问道∶『听说雪岩运粮到过杭州，不能进城又回上海。人呢？』『他一场大病，还没有好。不过，不要紧了。』七姑奶奶歉意地说∶『对不起，刘三叔，你现在还不能跟他见面；等我们把事情问清楚了再说。王抚台是不是真的殉节了？』『死得好，死得好！』凡事吊儿郎当，从没有什么事可以教他认真的刘不才，大声赞叹，『死得有价值。王抚台的官声，说实在的，没有啥好；这一来就只好不坏了，连长毛都佩服。』据刘不才说，杭州城陷那天，『忠王』李秀成单骑直奔巡抚衙门，原意是料到王有龄会殉节，想拦阻他不死；可是晚了一步，王有龄已朝服自缢于大堂右面的桂花树下。李秀成敬他忠义，解下尸首，停放在东辕门彭亭左侧，觅来上好棺木盛殓；王家上下老幼，自然置于保护之下。『长毛总算也有点人心。』七姑奶奶问道∶『不是说要拿王抚台的灵柩送到上海来吗？』『那倒没有听见说起。』
en: He changed the subject abruptly. “I hear Xueyan brought grain to Hangzhou but could not get it into the city and returned to Shanghai. Where is he?” “He has been very ill and is not fully recovered, though he is out of danger now.” The Seventh Lady spoke apologetically. “Forgive us, Third Uncle Liu, but you must not see him yet. Let us find out exactly what happened first. Did Governor Wang really die for his duty?” “A good death! A good death!” Liu, ordinarily so easy-going that nothing could make him take matters seriously, spoke with loud conviction. “A death that counted. To be honest, his reputation as an official was not particularly good. Now there can be nothing but good said of him. Even the rebels admire him.” According to Liu, on the day Hangzhou fell, Li Xiucheng, the Loyal King, rode alone straight to the governor’s yamen. Expecting Wang to take his own life, he had hoped to prevent it. But he was too late. Dressed in his court robes, Wang had already hanged himself from an osmanthus tree to the right of the main hall. Respecting his loyalty, Li had the body taken down and laid to the left of the pavilion by the eastern outer gate. He found a fine coffin for the burial preparations. Naturally, Wang’s household, old and young alike, was placed under protection. “The rebels have some humanity after all,” the Seventh Lady said. “Was there not talk of sending the coffin to Shanghai?” “I heard nothing of that.”

zh: 『满城呢？古应春问∶』将军瑞昌，大概也殉节了？『』满城在三天以后才破——。『在这三天中，李秀成暂停进攻，派人招降，条件相当宽大，准许旗人自由离去，准带随身细软以外，另发川资；同时将』天王『特赦杭州旗人的』诏旨『送给瑞昌看，目的是想消除他们的疑虑，而效用适得其反。也许是条件太宽大，反令人难以置信。而且，败军之将归旗，亦必定治罪，难逃一死；反倒失去了抚恤，甚至还褫籍，害得子孙不能抬头，无法生活，所以瑞昌与部将约定，决不投降。于是三天一过，李秀成下令攻击，驻防旗人，个个上阵，极力抵抗；满城周围九里，有五道城门，城上有红衣大炮，轰死了长毛三千多人，到十二月初一午后城破。将军瑞昌投荷花池而死；副都统杰纯、关福亦都自戕。男女老小纵火自焚以及投西湖而死的，不计其数。
en: “What of the Manchu quarter?” Gu asked. “General Ruichang must have died for his duty too?” “The Manchu quarter held out for another three days—” During those days, Li suspended his attacks and sent men to offer terms of surrender. The terms were generous. The bannermen would be allowed to leave freely, taking their portable valuables, and would receive travelling money as well. Ruichang was also shown an edict from the Heavenly King granting the Hangzhou bannermen a special pardon. The intention was to allay their fears, but it had the opposite effect. Perhaps the terms were so generous that they were difficult to believe. Besides, defeated officers returning to the banner establishment would certainly be punished. Death would be hard to escape; they would lose the compensation their families might otherwise receive and might even be struck from the banner rolls, leaving their descendants disgraced and without a livelihood. Ruichang and his officers therefore agreed never to surrender. Once the three days were over, Li ordered an assault. Every member of the garrison took up arms and resisted fiercely. The Manchu quarter had a circuit of nine li, five gates, and large hongyi cannon mounted on its walls. More than three thousand rebels were killed by their fire. It was not until the afternoon of the first day of the twelfth month that the quarter fell. Ruichang drowned himself in a lotus pond. The deputy banner commanders Jiechun and Guanfu also took their own lives. Countless men, women, and children died in fires they themselves had set or by throwing themselves into West Lake.

zh: 讲到这里，刘不才自我惊悸，面无人色；古应春赶紧叫人倒了热茶来，让他缓一缓气，再问他个人的遭遇。『杭州吃紧的时候，我正在那里。雪岩跟我商量，湖州亦已被围，总归一时回不去了；托我护送他的家眷到三天竺逃难。从此一别，就没有再见过他；因为后来看三天竺亦不是好地方，一步一步往里逃，真正菩萨保佑，逃到留下。』『留下』是个地名，在杭州西面；据说当初宋高宗迁都杭州，相度地势，起造宫殿，此处亦曾中意，嘱咐『留下』备选，所以叫做留下。其地多山，峰回泉绕，颇多隐秘之处，是逃难的好去处。『逃难的人很多，人多成市，就谈不到隐秘了。我一看情形不妙，跟雪岩夫人说∶』要逃得远，逃得深，越是荒凉穷苦的地方越好。雪岩夫人很有眼光，说我的话对。我就找到一处深山，真正人迹不到之处；最好的是有一道涧，有涧就有水，什么都不怕了。我雇人搭了一座茅棚，只有三尺高，下面铺上水板；又运上去七八担米，一缸盐菜，十来条火腿。说起来不相信，那时候杭州城里饿死的人，不知道多少。就我们那里没有一天不吃干饭。『』怪不得。刘三叔不象没饭吃的样子。『七姑奶奶说，』长毛倒没有寻到你们那里？『
en: At this point in his account, Liu himself grew frightened and pale. Gu quickly ordered hot tea so that he could recover his breath, then asked about his own experiences. “I happened to be in Hangzhou when the situation became critical. Xueyan discussed it with me. Huzhou was under siege too, so I could not return there for the time being. He asked me to escort his family to the three Tianzhu temples for refuge. We parted then, and I never saw him again. Later I decided that the temples were unsafe as well. We kept retreating farther into the countryside. Truly, the Bodhisattva protected us. We reached Liuxia.” Liuxia was a place west of Hangzhou. Its name meant “keep it.” According to tradition, when Emperor Gaozong of the Song moved his capital to Hangzhou and surveyed possible sites for a palace, this place pleased him, and he ordered it kept for consideration. Hence the name. With its hills, winding paths, streams, and many secluded places, it was well suited to sheltering refugees. “But there were so many refugees that a market sprang up. With all those people, there was no seclusion left. Seeing the danger, I told Xueyan’s wife that we must go farther and deeper into the hills: the more remote and impoverished the place, the better. She had good judgement and agreed. I found a spot deep in the mountains where people scarcely ever went. Best of all, there was a ravine with running water. Once we had water, there was nothing to fear. I hired men to build a thatched shelter, only three chi high, with boards laid underneath. Then I had seven or eight dan of rice, a jar of salted vegetables, and a dozen or so hams carried up. You may find it hard to believe: while untold numbers were starving in Hangzhou, we never went a day without solid rice.” “No wonder you do not look as though you have gone hungry,” said the Seventh Lady. “Did the rebels never find you?”

zh: 『差一点点。』刘不才说，『有一天我去赌钱——』『慢点。』七姑奶奶插嘴问道∶『逃难还有地方赌钱？』『不但赌钱，还有卖唱的呢！市面热闹得很。』市面是由逃难的人带来的。起先是有人搭个茅棚，卖些常用的杂物，没有字号，通称『小店』；然后小店成为茶店，作为聚会打听消息的所在；难中岁月，既愁且闷，少不得想个排遣之道，于是茶店又变成赌场。刘不才先是不愿与世隔绝，每天走七八里路到那个应运而生的市集中去听听新闻，到后来就专为去过赌瘾，牌九、做宝、掷骰子，什么都来；有庄做，就做庄家，没有庄做就赌下风，成了那家赌场的台柱。
en: “They nearly did. One day I went gambling—” “Wait a moment,” she interrupted. “Were there places to gamble even among the refugees?” “Not only gambling. There were singing entertainers too. The market was thriving.” It was the refugees who had created that market. At first someone had put up a thatched hut to sell everyday necessities. It had no business name and was simply called “the little shop.” Then it became a tea shop, where people gathered to hear the news. Refugee life was full of anxiety and boredom; people needed distraction, and the tea shop became a gambling house. At first Liu had walked seven or eight li to this new market each day merely to avoid losing contact with the world and to learn what was happening. Later he went chiefly to satisfy his appetite for gambling. Pai gow, the treasure game, dice—he played them all. If he could hold the bank, he did; otherwise he played against it. He became one of the gambling house’s mainstays.

zh: 这天午后，刘不才摊庄赌小牌九，手气极旺，往往他翻蹩十，重门也翻蹩十，算起来还有钱赢。正赌得兴头时，突然有人喊道∶『长毛来了！』刘不才不大肯相信，因为他上过一回当；有一次也是听说『长毛来了』，赌客仓皇走避，结果无事，但等回到赌场，台面上已空空如也。事后方知，是有人故意捣乱，好抢台面；他疑心这一次也是有人想趁火打劫，所以大家逃，他不逃，不慌不忙地收拾起自己的赌注再说。『刘三爷！』开赌场的过来警告∶『真的是长毛来了。』这一说刘不才方始着慌，匆匆将几十两银子塞入腰际，背起五六串铜钱，拔脚夺门而走。然而已经晚了，有两个长毛穷追不舍。刘不才虽急不乱，心里在想，自己衣服比别人穿得整齐；肩上又背着铜钱，长毛决不肯放过自己。这样一逃一追，到头来岂不是『引鬼进门』？念头转到此处，对付的办法也就有了；拉过一串铜钱来，将『串头绳』上的活结，一下扯开，『哗哗』地将一千铜元落得满地；然后跑几步，如法炮制。五六串铜钱撒完，肩上的重负全释，脚步就轻快了；然而还是不敢走正路，怕引长毛发现住处，兜了好大一个圈子，到晚上才绕道到家。
en: One afternoon he was banking at the small version of pai gow and enjoying extraordinary luck. Often he turned up a zero-point hand, only to find that the heavily backed opposing hand was also zero, so that he still came out ahead. At the height of the game, someone suddenly shouted, “The rebels are coming!” Liu was reluctant to believe it, having once been deceived by the same cry. On that occasion, the players had fled in panic and nothing had happened. When they returned, however, the gaming table had been stripped bare. They learned afterwards that someone had raised the false alarm to seize the money. Suspecting another attempt to profit from panic, Liu stayed while the others ran, calmly collecting his stakes. “Third Master Liu!” the proprietor warned him. “The rebels really are here.” Only then did Liu take fright. He hurriedly thrust several dozen taels into his waistband, slung five or six strings of copper cash over his shoulder, and bolted through the door. But it was already too late: two rebels pursued him relentlessly. Urgent though the danger was, he kept his head. His clothes were better than other people’s, and he had copper cash over his shoulder; they would never let him go. If he simply kept running, would he not lead the enemy to the family’s hiding place? Once he saw that, he knew what to do. He pulled a string of cash towards him, undid its slipknot, and sent a thousand coins clattering across the ground. After a few more strides he did the same again. When all five or six strings had been scattered, the weight was gone and he could run more lightly. Even so, he dared not take the direct route for fear of revealing their shelter. He made a long circuit and did not get home until evening.

zh: 『从那一次以后，胡老太太跟雪岩夫人就不准我再去赌了。其实，市面也就此打散了——那一次是一小队长毛，误打误撞闯到了那里；人数太少，不敢动手。第二天，还是第三天，来了大队人马，奸淫掳掠外加一把火；难民遭劫的不知多少？』刘不才说到这里，表情相当复杂，余悸余哀都犹在，却又似乎欣慰得意，『亏得我见机！这一宝总算让我看准了。』谈这样的生死大事，仍旧不脱赌徒的口吻，七姑奶奶对他又佩服，又好笑，但更多的是关切∶『以后始终没有遇见长毛？』『没有！不过好几次听见声音；提心吊胆的味道，只有尝过的人才晓得真不好受！』
en: “After that, Xueyan’s mother and wife forbade me to go gambling again. In any case, the market broke up. That first party was only a small detachment of rebels which had stumbled upon the place. There were too few of them to do much. The next day, or perhaps the day after, a large force came. They raped, looted, seized people, and finally set the place on fire. Who knows how many refugees suffered?” Liu’s expression was complicated. Fear and sorrow still lingered, yet he also looked relieved, even pleased with himself. “Luckily I saw what was coming. That was one wager I judged correctly.” Even discussing matters of life and death, he could not shed a gambler’s language. The Seventh Lady felt both admiration and amusement, but concern predominated. “You never met the rebels again after that?” “No. Several times we heard them, though. Only someone who has lived through it knows how dreadful that constant fear can be.”

zh: 然而，此刻提心吊胆的日子，也并不算完全过去。长毛进城，由于李秀成的约束，照例会有的烧、杀、奸、抢倒不甚厉害；但杭州人不肯从贼，男的上吊、女的投井、阖家自尽的，不计其数。这也不尽是忠义之气使然，而是生趣索然；其中又分成几类∶怕受辱吃苦头的是一类；满目极人间未有之惨，感情上承受不住，愿求解脱的，也是类；无衣无食，求苟延残喘而不可得，以为迟早是死，不如早死的，又是一类；历尽浩劫，到头来仍不免一场空，于心不甘，愤而自裁的，更是一类。象胡家这样『跳出劫数外，不在五行中』的；只怕十万人家找不出一家；然而现在却又在劫数中了。荒山茅棚，自然不能再住；最主要的原因是，存粮已罄，不能不全家『出山』；城里尸臭不可向迩，如果不是严冬，瘟疫早已流行，当然不能再住。好的是胡老太太本来信佛，自从胡雪岩平地一声雷，发达起来，更认定是菩萨保佑，大小庙宇庵堂，只要和尚尼姑上门化缘，必不会空手而回；三天竺是香火盛地，几座庙宇，无不相熟，找一处安顿下来，倒也容易。苦恼的仍旧是粮食。整个杭州城，全靠李秀成从嘉兴运来两万石米；如果不包括军食在内，倒也能维持一段时期，无奈先发军粮，再办平粜，老百姓的实惠就有限了。
en: Even now, the days of fear were not entirely over. Once the rebels entered Hangzhou, Li’s discipline kept the usual burning, killing, rape, and robbery from becoming too severe. Yet the people of Hangzhou were unwilling to submit. Men hanged themselves, women threw themselves into wells, and whole families took their own lives in countless numbers. This was not entirely an expression of loyalty to the dynasty. Many had lost all desire to live, for different reasons. Some feared humiliation and suffering. Some had seen horrors beyond anything they could emotionally endure and sought release. Others had neither clothes nor food and could find no means of prolonging their lives; believing death inevitable, they chose it sooner rather than later. Still others, having survived terrible calamities only to find everything lost in the end, killed themselves in bitter despair. Among a hundred thousand households, perhaps not one had escaped the catastrophe as the Hu family had. Yet now calamity threatened them again. They could no longer remain in their mountain hut, chiefly because their food was exhausted and the whole family had to come down. The city was uninhabitable: the stench of bodies made it impossible to approach. Had it not been the depths of winter, epidemic disease would already have spread. Fortunately, Hu’s mother had always been devout. Since her son’s sudden rise in the world, she had been more convinced than ever of the Bodhisattva’s protection. Monks and nuns who came soliciting donations for temples, large or small, never left her empty-handed. The three Tianzhu temples were an important centre of worship, and she knew them all. Finding a place to stay was therefore easy enough. The difficulty was still food. All Hangzhou depended on twenty thousand shi of rice that Li had brought from Jiaxing. Without the troops’ needs, it might have lasted some time. But the army received its rations first, and only afterwards was grain sold to civilians at controlled prices. The benefit to ordinary people was limited.

zh: 『现在全家大小，每天只吃一顿粥。我倒还好，就是上面老的，下小的，不能不想法子。』『这个法子总想得出。』古应春说，『不过，刘三叔，你有句话我不懂；你一向胃口很好，每天吃一顿粥，倒能支持得住？还说「还好」！』刘不才笑笑，不好意思地答道∶『我会到长毛公馆里去打野食。』七姑奶奶也笑了，『刘三叔，你真正是，老虎嘴里的食，也敢夺来吃。』她说，『你怎么打法？』『这就不好告诉你了。闲话少说，有句正经话，我要跟你们商量，有个王八蛋来找雪岩的麻烦；如果不理他会出事。』刘不才口中的『王八蛋』叫袁忠清，是钱塘县署理知县。此人原来是袁甲三部下的一个『勇目』，打仗发了笔横财，活动袁甲三的一个幕友，在一次『保案』中将他添上了一个名字，得了『六品蓝翎』的功名。后来犯了军令，袁甲三要杀他；吓得连夜开了小差，逃回江西原籍。
en: “Now the whole household, old and young, has only one meal of gruel a day. I can manage, but something must be done for the old people and the children.” “We shall find a way,” Gu said. “But there is something I do not understand, Third Uncle Liu. You have always had a good appetite. How can you keep going on one meal of gruel a day and still say you can manage?” Liu smiled a little sheepishly. “I find ways to get a meal at the rebels’ residences.” The Seventh Lady laughed too. “You really would snatch food from a tiger’s mouth! How do you manage it?” “That I cannot tell you. Let us leave idle talk aside. There is something serious I must discuss with you. A bastard is making trouble for Xueyan. If he is ignored, something will happen.” The “bastard” was Yuan Zhongqing, acting magistrate of Qiantang County. He had originally been a petty militia commander under Yuan Jiasan. After making a windfall from the war, he worked through one of Yuan’s advisers to have his name added to a list of men recommended for honours. He obtained sixth-rank status and the right to wear a blue feather. Later he violated military orders, and Yuan Jiasan intended to execute him. Terrified, he deserted overnight and fled to his native Jiangxi.

zh: 那时的江西巡抚是何桂清的同年、穆彰阿的得意门生张芾；袁忠清假报为六品蓝翎的县丞，又走了门路，投效在张芾那里。不久，长毛攻江西省城，南昌老百姓，竭力助守，使得张芾大起好感；爱屋及乌，便宜了『忘八蛋』，竟被委为制造局帮办军装。这是个极肥的差使，在袁忠清手里更是左右逢源，得其所哉。不久，由于宁国之捷，专案报奖，张芾倒很照顾袁忠清，特意嘱咐幕友，为他加上很好的考语，保升县令。这原是一个大喜讯，在他人当然会高兴不得了，而袁忠清不但愁眉苦脸，甚至坐卧不宁。同事不免奇怪，少不得有人问他∶『老袁，指日高升！上头格外照应你，不是列个字的泛泛保举；你是十六个字的考语，京里一定照准。眼看就是「百里侯」；如何倒象如丧考妣似的。』『说什么指日高升？不吃官司，只怕都要靠祖宗积德。』接着，又摇摇着∶『官司吃定了！祖宗积德也没用。』他那同事大为惊惑∶『为什么？』袁忠清先还不敢说，经不起那同事诚恳热心，拍胸脯担保，必定设法为他分忧，袁忠清才吐露了心底的秘密。『实不相瞒，我这个「六品蓝翎」，货真价实；县丞是个「西贝货」。你想这一保上去，怎么得了？』
en: The governor of Jiangxi at that time was Zhang Fu, a fellow graduate of He Guiqing’s examination year and a favourite pupil of Muzhang’a. Yuan falsely represented himself as a sixth-rank county assistant magistrate entitled to the blue feather. Through further connections, he secured a position under Zhang. Before long, the rebels attacked Nanchang, the provincial capital. The people of Nanchang threw themselves into its defence, winning Zhang’s warm regard. That goodwill extended to their fellow native, and the “bastard” benefited: he was appointed to assist with military supplies at the manufacturing bureau. It was an extremely lucrative post, and Yuan found opportunities for profit on every side. Soon afterwards, the victory at Ningguo occasioned a special recommendation for honours. Zhang took particular care of Yuan, telling his advisers to give him an excellent assessment and recommend him for promotion to county magistrate. Ordinarily this would have been wonderful news. Anyone else would have been delighted. Yuan, however, looked miserable and could neither sit nor rest in peace. His colleagues naturally wondered why. “Yuan, promotion is just ahead of you! The authorities have taken special care. This is no routine recommendation with a token appraisal; yours runs to sixteen characters. The capital is sure to approve it. You are about to rule a county. Why look as though you have lost both parents?” “Promotion? It will take all the merit my ancestors accumulated to keep me from a criminal charge.” Then he shook his head. “No, the charge is certain. Even my ancestors’ merit will not help.” His colleague was astonished. “Why?” At first Yuan dared not explain. But the man was so earnest and helpful, solemnly promising to find a way out, that Yuan finally revealed his secret. “To be frank, my sixth rank and blue feather are perfectly genuine. The county assistant magistracy is a fake. What will happen when this recommendation goes up?”

zh: 『什么？你的县丞是假的！』假的就不能见天日。江西的保案上去，吏部自然要查案；袁忠清因为是县丞才能保知县，知则先要问他这个县丞是什么『班子』？一查无案可稽；就要行文来问。试问袁忠清可拿得出『部照「或是捐过班的』实收『？象这种假冒的事，不是没有；史部的书办十九是吃人不吐骨头的积年滑吏，无弊不悉，只怕没有缝钻，一旦拿住了短处，予取予求勒索够了，怕还是要办他个』假冒职官『的罪名，落个充军的下场。他那同事，倒也言而有信，为他请教高人，想出一条路子，补捐一个县丞。军兴以来，为了筹饷，大开捐例，各省都向吏部先领到大批空白收据；即名为『实收』——捐班有各种花样，各种折扣，以实际捐纳银数，掣给收据，就叫『实收』，将来据以换领正式部照；所以这倒容易，兑了银子，立时可以办妥。但是，日期不符也不行；缴验『实收』，一看是保案以后所捐，把戏立刻拆穿。『这没有别的办法，只有托人情。』『托人情要钱，我知道。』袁忠清说，『我这个差使虽有点油水，平时都结交了朋友；吃过用过，也就差不多了。如今，都在这里了！』将枕头箱打开，里面银票倒是不少，但零零碎碎加起来，不过百把两银子；象这种倒填年月的花样，担着极大的干系，少说说也得三百两，他那朋友知道袁忠清是有意做作；事到如今，人家半吊子，自己不能做为德不卒的事，只好替他添上五十两银子，跟『前途』好说歹说，将他这件事办了下来。
en: “What? You are not really an assistant magistrate?” A false appointment could not stand scrutiny. Once Jiangxi’s recommendation reached the Ministry of Personnel, the records would naturally be checked. Yuan was being recommended for county magistrate because he supposedly held an assistant magistracy. The first question would be how he had obtained that appointment. Finding no record, the ministry would send an enquiry. Could Yuan produce an official certificate or a receipt for a purchased appointment? Such impostures were not unknown. Almost all the ministry’s clerks were old hands at extortion, knowing every variety of fraud and forever looking for an opening. Once they had discovered his weakness, they would demand whatever they pleased. Even after extracting enough money, they might still charge him with falsely claiming official status and have him sent into military exile. His colleague proved as good as his word. After consulting someone knowledgeable, he found a solution: Yuan could purchase an assistant magistracy now. Since the war began, the government had greatly expanded the sale of appointments to raise military funds. Each province had received large quantities of blank receipts from the Ministry of Personnel. These were called receipts for the actual amount paid. There were many schemes and discounts for purchasing appointments; the receipt stated the silver actually contributed and could later be exchanged for a formal ministry certificate. Paying the silver and obtaining a receipt was easy enough. The difficulty was the date. If the receipt showed that the appointment had been purchased after the recommendation, the deception would be exposed at once. “There is only one way. We must call in a favour.” “And favours cost money. I know,” Yuan replied. “My post yields a little, but I have spent it on cultivating friends. After food and expenses, there is not much left. Everything I have is here.” He opened a small chest kept by his pillow. It contained quite a few banknotes, but all the little sums together came to only a hundred taels or so. Backdating a receipt was a serious risk and would cost at least three hundred. His friend knew that Yuan was putting on a performance. But having taken the matter this far, he could hardly abandon a good deed halfway through merely because Yuan was unreliable. He added fifty taels of his own and, after much pleading with the people handling the business, got it arranged.
